classification_rules.released_checkpoint_route: evaluate lego.ckpt / lego_rt.ckpt (final, epoch 249) on the natively regenerated 40-view validation set through the unchanged Lightning validate path: REPRODUCED if |view-mean PSNR - Table 1| <= 1.0 dB for both variants, COMPARABLE if <= 2.0 dB, otherwise DISCREPANT (to be attributed). 1.0 dB covers the observed run/val-set spread (worklog 33: 0.5 dB between identical-config runs) plus final-vs-best (released logs: best 33.94 vs Table 34.09)
classification_rules.training_route: if the 400-view set is generated: train lego_vis.yml and lego_vis_rt.yml unchanged (seed 0, 250 epochs); REPRODUCED if the logged best val_psnr is within 1.0 dB of Table 1 and the final within 1.0 dB of the released final checkpoint's value on the same validation set; COMPARABLE within 2.0 dB
classification_rules.fig8_route: masked LDR PSNR of the lego_cmp frames is reported as COMPARABLE only (unpublished protocol)
classification_rules.performance: path-tracer timings (Fig. 6/7) are BLOCKED: the production renderer is not released; PyTorch/deferred timings are reported separately and never compared with them

N1_reference_noise.question: does 1024-spp validation-target noise (released config) vs the paper's 4096-spp data explain the larger HQ gap?
N1_reference_noise.design: rr_run.py with RR_SEED=1234 seeds torch/numpy/random before the unchanged generator; generate 8 validation views twice with config copies differing ONLY in sample_count (1024 vs 4096) and num_images 8 (identical cameras/lights; Cycles' fixed seed makes the 1024 samples a prefix of the 4096 estimate, so the two targets are positively correlated - reported, it understates the noise difference); evaluate released HQ and small on both
N1_reference_noise.rule: if view-mean PSNR(HQ vs 4096) - PSNR(HQ vs 1024) >= 1.0 dB, target noise accounts for a material part of the HQ gap; < 0.3 dB: not explanatory; between: partial

amendments.training_data: the 400-view training set follows the released generate_Lego.yml (1024 spp), not the paper's 4096 spp; declared, not changed
